spec_match.rationale: Checks the CSS Fonts 4 equivalences the rename depends on: the nine-keyword percentage mapping evaluated from computed style, property aliasing set-one-read-both in both directions, and width-descriptor-range face selection proven with measured narrow/wide instances.

interactive.rationale: Three buttons each execute real engine evaluations: computed-style table fill, two-direction alias check, and live face registration + measurement.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises keywords, two-direction aliasing, FontFace aliasing (covered here via the probe page link plus descriptor parse readout), and narrow-vs-wide face selection — delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: The dropped-declaration branch (font-width unparsed) renders explicitly; the face-selection verdict has a real failure branch keyed to the measured ratio; parser retention of each descriptor spelling is reported per face.

references.rationale: Links the CSS Fonts 4 keyword mapping table and both sibling concepts; the feature index carries the ChromeStatus link.

conformance.rationale: The suite covers descriptor parse (new fails honestly pre-153, legacy passes) and the axis-driving contract; the lab's keyword and selection checks extend those with measured evidence.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP driver run 2026-08-16 after the measurement-span fix (f2-lab.png): keyword table computed 50%…87.5% exactly per spec, alias check showed font-width dropped (pre-153) while font-stretch computed 66%, and face selection measured 97px vs 390px (ratio 4.02×, verdict: selection works); zero console errors.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts font-width-keyword-table-ran, font-width-alias-check-ran (with the accepted boolean), and font-width-face-selection-measured with the observed ratio.

design_system.rationale: Variables only; samples are black-on-ivory; results are charcoal-on-stone monospace blocks.

accessibility.rationale: Semantic mapping table with scoped headers in a focusable scroll region, output elements tied to their buttons, and text verdicts not colour-only.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Feature harness passed both classes; sample cards stack via auto-fit grid and wide lines scroll inside their cards at 360px.

openQuestions.title: Confirm both descriptor spellings are retained together on Chrome 153
openQuestions.detail: Pre-153 the parser keeps only font-stretch (observed and rendered honestly). On a 153 build, verify each @font-face rule retains/reflects the font-width spelling too and that selection still measures ≈4× — including whether the later font-width declaration overrides the earlier font-stretch one in the same rule, which the alias model implies.

guidanceConsulted.query: css property alias migration testing computed style
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Verify aliases through computed style rather than assuming specified-value equivalence, and surface dropped declarations.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Every equivalence is read back from getComputedStyle or CSSOM; a dropped font-width declaration is reported as exactly that, never inferred as equivalent.

guidanceConsulted.query: announcing results of on-demand test runs
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Route asynchronous result text into output/status elements associated with their triggering controls.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All three panels write plain-text results into output elements with for= references to their buttons.

summary: The migration lab: spec keyword mapping confirmed live, the pre-153 dropped font-width property surfaced honestly, and width-range face selection proven with a measured 4.02× narrow/wide ratio from real registered fonts.
